quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Getting up bright and early, before most people are even awake"?
quests.hint: Think about when someone would need to wake up if they're up before everyone else.
quests.explanation: Yes! Waking up early like this happens at the start of the day. People who love mornings are sometimes called 'early birds'!
quests.funFact: This comes from the saying 'the early bird catches the worm'!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Someone who feels most awake and alert once everyone else has gone to bed"?
quests.hint: Think about what 'once everyone else has gone to bed' tells you about the time.
quests.explanation: Yes! Feeling most awake once others are asleep happens at night. People like this are sometimes called 'night owls'!
quests.funFact: Real owls are famously wide awake and active at night!

quests.instruction: "An early riser who loves greeting each new morning with a smile" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'morning' — which part of the day is that?
quests.explanation: Yes! Greeting the morning happens right as the day begins.
quests.funFact: Some people naturally feel most awake and cheerful in the morning!

quests.instruction: "Someone who stays up very late working hard on a big project" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about what 'staying up very late' tells you about the time.
quests.explanation: Yes! Staying up very late happens at night. This is sometimes called 'burning the midnight oil'!
quests.funFact: This old saying comes from a time when people used oil lamps to see while working late!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "Someone who feels most energetic and cheerful right after waking up". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about what 'right after waking up' tells you about the time.
quests.explanation: Yes! Waking up happens at the start of the day. Someone like this is sometimes called a 'morning person'!
quests.funFact: Scientists say everyone has a natural body clock that affects when they feel most awake!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "Falling into a deep, heavy sleep the moment your head hits the pillow". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when your head would actually be resting on a pillow.
quests.explanation: Yes! Falling asleep on a pillow like this happens at night. People sometimes say they 'sleep like a log'!
quests.funFact: A truly deep sleep is one of the most important parts of feeling rested the next day!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A cheerful wake-up call meant to get someone up and moving quickly". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when someone would need a wake-up call in the first place.
quests.explanation: Yes! A wake-up call happens in the morning, as the day begins. People often say 'rise and shine!'
quests.funFact: This cheerful phrase has been used to wake people up for over 100 years!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A gentle rhyme said to a child right as they're tucked in to sleep". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when a child would be getting tucked in for sleep.
quests.explanation: Yes! Being tucked in to sleep happens at night. A classic rhyme said then is 'sleep tight'!
quests.funFact: This old rhyme is hundreds of years old and is still said by families today!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A hard worker who stays busy from morning until the afternoon, like a busy bee"?
quests.hint: Think about the span of time between morning and afternoon.
quests.explanation: Yes! Morning through afternoon is all part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: Real bees are famously hardworking, visiting up to a hundred flowers on one trip!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Someone who does their best thinking once the house is finally quiet and dark"?
quests.hint: Think about when a house would finally become quiet and dark.
quests.explanation: Yes! A quiet, dark house means everyone has settled in for the night.
quests.funFact: Some people find it easier to focus once all the daytime noise and activity has quieted down!

quests.instruction: "Someone who focuses best with bright, natural sunlight streaming through a window" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when natural sunlight actually streams through a window.
quests.explanation: Yes! Natural sunlight only streams through windows during the day.
quests.funFact: Studies show natural light can actually help people focus and feel more alert!

quests.instruction: "A classic phrase used to begin a story read right before sleep" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when a story like this is usually read to someone.
quests.explanation: Yes! Stories read right before sleep happen at night. Many classic tales begin with 'once upon a time'!
quests.funFact: This famous phrase has been used to start fairy tales for hundreds of years!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A classic saying about making the very most of the sunlight you're given". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about what you'd need in order to make the most of sunlight.
quests.explanation: Yes! Sunlight is a daytime thing. This idea is often expressed with the saying 'seize the day'!
quests.funFact: This famous phrase comes from an old Latin saying that's over 2,000 years old!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A grandparent's gentle reminder that it's finally time to settle in for bed, stars and all". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'stars' — when do we usually see them?
quests.explanation: Yes! Stars and bedtime both point to nighttime.
quests.funFact: Grandparents in many cultures have their own special bedtime traditions and sayings!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "An airline pilot flying a full plane to its sunny destination"?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'sunny' — it's a strong clue about the light outside.
quests.explanation: Yes! A sunny destination tells you it's daytime.
quests.funFact: Airline pilots have to check the weather carefully before every single flight!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "An airline pilot flying a red-eye flight through the dark sky"?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'dark' — it's a clue about the sky.
quests.explanation: Yes! A dark sky tells you it's nighttime. A 'red-eye flight' is a flight that travels through the night!
quests.funFact: This kind of flight is called a 'red-eye' because passengers often arrive tired with red, sleepy eyes!

quests.instruction: "A window display being arranged in a busy shop for customers to see" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when shops are usually open and busy with customers.
quests.explanation: Yes! Shops are usually busy with customers and displays during the day.
quests.funFact: Store window displays are carefully designed to catch a shopper's eye!

quests.instruction: "A late movie ending and ushers sweeping up popcorn in an empty theater" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'late' — what part of the day does that suggest?
quests.explanation: Yes! A late movie ending suggests it's already nighttime.
quests.funFact: Movie theaters clean between every single showing to get ready for the next audience!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A tour guide leading visitors through a sunlit museum". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about what's lighting up the museum halls so brightly.
quests.explanation: Yes! A sunlit museum tells you it's daytime.
quests.funFact: Some museums have skylights specially built to let in natural daylight!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A radio host playing calm music for listeners driving home very late". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when roads are usually quiet, with just a few drivers left.
quests.explanation: Yes! Driving home very late suggests it's already nighttime.
quests.funFact: Some radio stations play calm, quiet music specifically for late-night listeners!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A dentist checking a patient's teeth during a scheduled appointment"?
quests.hint: Think about when most dentist appointments are usually scheduled.
quests.explanation: Yes! Dentist appointments are usually scheduled during the day.
quests.funFact: Dentists recommend a checkup about twice a year to keep teeth healthy!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A baker's oven glowing warmly hours before the sun comes up"?
quests.hint: Think about what 'before the sun comes up' tells you — has the day begun yet?
quests.explanation: Yes! 'Before the sun comes up' means the day hasn't started yet, so it's still nighttime.
quests.funFact: Bread needs hours to rise and bake, which is why some bakers start so early!

quests.instruction: "A barber trimming hair in a bright, bustling shop" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'bright' — what does it tell you about the shop?
quests.explanation: Yes! A bright, bustling shop tells you it's daytime.
quests.funFact: Barbershops have been a place for haircuts and friendly chats for hundreds of years!

quests.instruction: "A 24-hour diner serving warm soup to a few quiet customers" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when a diner would be quiet, with only a few customers inside.
quests.explanation: Yes! A quiet diner with few customers suggests it's very late at night.
quests.funFact: Some diners stay open all day and all night, so they never have to lock their doors!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A photographer snapping pictures of children playing in the park". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when children are usually playing outside at the park.
quests.explanation: Yes! Children usually play at the park during the day.
quests.funFact: Photographers often say the best natural light happens in the early morning or late afternoon!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A janitor mopping the school hallways long after students have gone home". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about what 'long after students have gone home' tells you about the time.
quests.explanation: Yes! This cleaning happens well after school hours, once it's evening or night.
quests.funFact: School janitors often work hard behind the scenes to keep classrooms clean and ready!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A park ranger leading a nature hike along a sunny trail"?
quests.hint: Think about when a nature hike would have plenty of light to follow the trail.
quests.explanation: Yes! A sunny trail tells you it's daytime.
quests.funFact: Park rangers help protect wildlife and teach visitors how to explore safely!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A comet-watcher setting an alarm to catch a rare event high in the dark sky"?
quests.hint: Think about when a rare sky event like this would actually be visible.
quests.explanation: Yes! A dark sky tells you it's nighttime, perfect for spotting a comet.
quests.funFact: Comets are made of ice and dust, and some only pass by Earth once every many years!

quests.instruction: "A construction worker following blueprints under the open sky" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when construction work is usually done, under bright light.
quests.explanation: Yes! Construction work is usually done during the day, under an open sky.
quests.funFact: Blueprints get their blue color from an old copying process used to print building plans!

quests.instruction: "A zookeeper checking on nocturnal animals in a dimly lit exhibit" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'nocturnal' — what does that word mean?
quests.explanation: Yes! Nocturnal animals are most active at night, so this checkup happens then.
quests.funFact: Some zoos flip the lighting for nocturnal animals so visitors can see them awake during the day!
